title: Protesters in Delhi demand FIR against police officer for alleged molestation
seoTitle: Delhi protest against alleged police molestation

tea.why: Protesters gathered after a police officer was accused of molesting a woman journalist during a previous protest.
tea.want: They demanded the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) against the police officer.
tea.changed: Oct 5: A Delhi court granted bail to 17 arrested protesters and requested a report on alleged custodial torture.

summary: On October 5, protesters gathered outside the Parliament Street police station in Delhi to demand the registration of an FIR against a police officer. The officer was accused of molesting a woman journalist during an earlier protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi Police arrested 17 individuals, including students and journalists, on charges of unlawful assembly, obstructing public space, and assaulting police personnel. A Delhi court later granted bail to the arrested individuals and requested a report from the Deputy Commissioner of Police regarding allegations of custodial torture made by two of the protesters. The court also directed the preservation of CCTV footage from the police station.
demands: Registration of an FIR against the police officer accused of molesting a woman journalist
response: Delhi Police registered a case against 17 protesters for unlawful assembly, obstruction, and assaulting police. A Delhi court granted bail to the 17 arrested individuals and sought a report from the DCP New Delhi regarding allegations of custodial torture, also directing the preservation of CCTV footage.

arrests.text: 17 students and journalists were taken into police custody (1)

injuries.text: One police official allegedly sustained injuries (1); some arrested persons also sustained injuries (1, 2)

updates.text: Protesters gathered outside the Parliament Street police station in Delhi to demand an FIR against a police officer.
Delhi Police arrested 17 individuals, including students and journalists, on charges including unlawful assembly and obstructing a public area.
A police official reportedly sustained injuries during the protest, according to the investigating officer.
Two arrested protesters alleged custodial torture, and some accused sustained injuries.
A Delhi court granted bail to all 17 arrested individuals.
The court requested a report from the DCP New Delhi regarding the custodial torture allegations and ordered the preservation of CCTV footage.
The court also directed that necessary medical treatment be provided to the injured accused.
